Q: Using git submodules as poor mans git lfs A:

If you want the remote to stay lean (just plain ssh with static .git folder), use submodule, the complexity is mostly on the client side, you need to make sure to do git submodule update/init --remote/--merge foreach when you are modifying them. If you make changes, you must make sure to commit in both submodule, and the parent repo, and all the large file will have their own version history. The upside is that your remote is just two folders, A.git, and A-large-file.git, that were both initialized with a git init --bare.

If you want the client side to be simple, with just one repo, but allowing them to easily choose what large file to check out, then LFS is suitable, the client just need to do: git lfs track "large-file.bin", git add .gitattributes git add largefile2.bin`, just one repo for the client. The downside is the remote need a dedicated LFS server, in addition to plain ssh and static .git folder.

My own workflow is submodule, because i can just grab any old laptop and set up an SSH server on my home network, create two git folders, and manage large file on the client side, no HTTP or NAT traversal or ISP restriction to manage. If I am distributing files to client, I will set up dedicated LFS on a cloud hosting provider , so users only need to run git clone once, and not having to worry about submodule's intricated syntax.

Either way, one side has to bear the complexity.

Q: Signal doesn't update when creating a new array of objects A:

Looks like classic Angular signals immutability issue. You’re mutating/deriving from the same reference, so the signal doesn’t detect a change.

Signals only react when the reference changes not when you modify inside the array.

Instead of:

this.uploadedFiles().push(newFile)

Do:

this.uploadedFiles.set([...this.uploadedFiles(), newFile])

Same applies when removing/editing always return a new array. Also, if you’re mapping objects, make sure you’re not reusing the same object references internally.

No mutation, always new reference -> signals update properly.

Q: Can't get two DbContexts to work in same ASP.NET Core solution with EF Core / SQL Server A:

It is due to closures: What are 'closures' in .NET?.

You can see simple explanation in this post - the variable outside the callback is just the field on the object that represents the closure. And both callbacks' closures will refer to that.

Then, by changing that variable connectionString, you are changing it on object representing the closure, so both callbacks see the change.

That is why creating another variable will solve the problem, there will be different field for each callback.

Q: Resource punkt not found. Please use the NLTK Downloader to obtain the resource: >>> import nltk >>> nltk.download('punkt') A:

I was trying to use NLTK’s sentence tokenizer, but I kept getting SSL certificate errors when downloading resources:

Code

[nltk_data] Error loading punkt: <urlopen error [SSL:
[nltk_data]     CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed:
[nltk_data]     unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1081)>
[nltk_data] Error loading punkt_tab: <urlopen error [SSL:
[nltk_data]     CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed:
[nltk_data]     unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1081)>
[nltk_data] Error loading wordnet: <urlopen error [SSL:
[nltk_data]     CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed:
[nltk_data]     unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1081)>
[nltk_data] Error loading omw-1.4: <urlopen error [SSL:
[nltk_data]     CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed:
[nltk_data]     unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1081)>

When try to downloading punkt, I still saw errors mentioning punkt_tab.

Solution

The issue was resolved by forcing Python to use an unverified SSL context when downloading NLTK data. Here’s the working code:

python

import ssl
import nltk

try:
    _create_unverified_https_context = ssl._create_unverified_context
except AttributeError:
    # Legacy Python that doesn’t verify HTTPS
    pass
else:
    ssl._create_default_https_context = _create_unverified_https_context

# Download required resources
nltk.download('punkt')
nltk.download('wordnet')
nltk.download('omw-1.4')
# Note: 'punkt_tab' is not actually needed, but included here if your environment references it
nltk.download('punkt_tab')
